lesson_scope: Basic complex loci in the Argand plane: circles |z - z_0| = r, perpendicular bisectors |z - z_1| = |z - z_2|, half-lines (rays) arg(z - z_0) = alpha, Cartesian conversions, simultaneous intersections, and geometric locus transformations (z^2 and 1/z).

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Identifying centre and radius of circle locus and testing origin containment.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Circle centre and radius identification.

hints: Distance from centre to origin is $\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2} = 5$, which matches radius.

walkthrough.text:
Identify centre and radius:
$$|z - (3 - 4\mathrm{i})| = 5 \implies \text{Centre } = 3 - 4\mathrm{i}, \quad \text{Radius } = 5$$

Check origin:
$$|0 - (3 - 4\mathrm{i})| = |-3 + 4\mathrm{i}| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + 4^2} = 5$$
$$\text{Since distance from centre to origin equals radius, the origin lies on the circle.}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Cartesian equation of perpendicular bisector locus.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Perpendicular bisector Cartesian equation.

walkthrough.text:
Simplify to linear form:
$$-4x + 4 = -12y + 36 \implies 12y = 4x + 32 \implies y = \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{8}{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Half-line locus initial point and Cartesian equation with domain.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Ray initial point and linear equation with domain.

walkthrough.text:
Identify initial point and angle:
$$\text{Initial point } = 1 + 2\mathrm{i} \implies (1, 2), \quad \theta = \frac{\pi}{4}$$

Derive Cartesian line equation with domain restriction:
$$m = \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$$
$$y - 2 = 1(x - 1) \implies y = x + 1 \quad (x > 1)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Finding axis intercepts of a circle locus.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding real axis intercepts of circle.

walkthrough.text:
Write Cartesian equation and set $y = 0$:
$$(x - 4)^2 + (0 - 3)^2 = 25 \implies (x - 4)^2 + 9 = 25$$
$$(x - 4)^2 = 16$$

Solve for $x$:
$$x - 4 = \pm 4 \implies x = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 8$$
$$\text{Intersection points: } (0, 0) \text{ and } (8, 0)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Midpoint, perpendicular gradient, and perpendicular bisector equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Midpoint and perpendicular bisector equation.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate midpoint and segment gradient:
$$\text{Midpoint } M = \frac{(-2 + \mathrm{i}) + (4 + 5\mathrm{i})}{2} = 1 + 3\mathrm{i} \implies (1, 3)$$
$$m_{AB} = \frac{5 - 1}{4 - (-2)} = \frac{2}{3} \implies m_\perp = -\frac{3}{2}$$

Form perpendicular bisector equation:
$$y - 3 = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 1) \implies 2y - 6 = -3x + 3 \implies 3x + 2y - 9 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds gradient of $AB = \frac{2}{3}$ and perpendicular gradient $-\frac{3}{2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Point intersection of origin-circle and ray locus.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Intersection of circle and ray locus.

walkthrough.text:
Apply polar to Cartesian conversion:
$$z = 4\left(\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)$$

Evaluate exact values:
$$z = 4\left(-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mathrm{i}\right) = -2 + 2\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Circle expanded equation and horizontal tangent lines.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Expanded polynomial circle equation.

walkthrough.text:
Write standard circle equation:
$$(x - 3)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = (2\sqrt{2})^2 = 8$$

Expand and collect terms:
$$x^2 - 6x + 9 + y^2 - 4y + 4 = 8$$
$$x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 4y + 5 = 0$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding extremal horizontal tangents.

hints: Horizontal tangents occur at $y = y_0 \pm R$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the highest and lowest $y$-values on the circle:
$$\text{Centre } y_0 = 2, \quad \text{Radius } R = 2\sqrt{2}$$
$$y = 2 \pm 2\sqrt{2}$$

State the equations of horizontal tangents:
$$y = 2 + 2\sqrt{2} \quad \text{and} \quad y = 2 - 2\sqrt{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Perpendicular bisector equation and real/imaginary intercepts.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving Cartesian line equation of bisector.
Finding purely real and purely imaginary points on locus.

walkthrough.text:
Find purely imaginary point ($x = 0$):
$$2(0) + y - 6 = 0 \implies y = 6 \implies z = 6\mathrm{i}$$

Find purely real point ($y = 0$):
$$2x + 0 - 6 = 0 \implies x = 3 \implies z = 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Half-line locus equation and circle intersection.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Ray equation and domain determination.

hints: Initial point is $(-2, 2)$ and gradient is $\tan(-\pi/4) = -1$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify endpoint and gradient:
$$\text{Initial point } = -2 + 2\mathrm{i} \implies (-2, 2)$$
$$m = \tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -1$$

Form line equation:
$$y - 2 = -1(x + 2) \implies y = -x \quad (x > -2)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Intersection of ray and origin circle.

hints: $2x^2 = 8 \implies x^2 = 4 \implies x = 2$ (since $x > -2$ and endpoint $x = -2$ is excluded).

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $y = -x$ into $|z|^2 = 8$:
$$x^2 + (-x)^2 = 8 \implies 2x^2 = 8 \implies x^2 = 4$$

Select root in domain $x > -2$:
$$x = 2 \implies y = -2 \implies z = 2 - 2\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Note: } x = -2 \text{ corresponds to the open endpoint, which is excluded.}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Circle and perpendicular bisector intersection and distance.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving line equation y = x for bisector.

walkthrough.text:
Expand squared distances:
$$(x - 3)^2 + y^2 = x^2 + (y - 3)^2$$
$$x^2 - 6x + 9 + y^2 = x^2 + y^2 - 6y + 9$$

Simplify:
$$-6x = -6y \implies y = x$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding intersection points and distance.

walkthrough.text:
Solve simultaneously with $x^2 + y^2 = 25$:
$$x^2 + x^2 = 25 \implies 2x^2 = 25 \implies x = \pm \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}$$

State intersection points and compute diameter distance:
$$P_1 = \left(\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}, \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}\right), \quad P_2 = \left(-\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}, -\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$$
$$\text{Distance } = 2R = 2(5) = 10$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Circular arc locus and transformation under w = z^2.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Geometric description of circular arc locus and arc length.

hints: Locus of $z$ is a circular arc centred at origin with radius $2$.

walkthrough.text:
Describe the locus of $z$:
$$\text{Circular arc centred at the origin with radius } r = 2$$
$$\text{Angle span: } \Delta\theta = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}$$

Calculate arc length:
$$L = r\Delta\theta = 2\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: States circular arc centred at origin with radius $2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Transformed locus of z^2 and transformed arc length.

walkthrough.text:
Determine modulus and argument range of $w = z^2$:
$$|w| = |z|^2 = 4$$
$$\arg(w) = 2\arg(z) \implies 2\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \leqslant \arg(w) \leqslant 2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \implies \frac{\pi}{3} \leqslant \arg(w) \leqslant \pi$$

Calculate transformed arc length:
$$\Delta\phi = \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}$$
$$L_w = 4\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{8\pi}{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Transformation w = 1/z on a line locus producing a circle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deriving u^2 + v^2 = u for inversion locus.

walkthrough.text:
Express $w$ in Cartesian components:
$$w = \frac{1}{1 + \mathrm{i}y} = \frac{1 - \mathrm{i}y}{1 + y^2} = \frac{1}{1 + y^2} - \mathrm{i}\frac{y}{1 + y^2}$$
$$u = \frac{1}{1 + y^2}, \quad v = -\frac{y}{1 + y^2}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Identifying circle centre, radius, and excluded origin for 1/z locus.

walkthrough.text:
Complete the square on $u^2 - u + v^2 = 0$:
$$\left(u - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{4} + v^2 = 0 \implies \left(u - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + v^2 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2$$

Describe locus geometrically:
$$\text{Circle centred at } \left(\frac{1}{2}, 0\right) \text{ with radius } \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Since } u = \frac{1}{1+y^2} > 0 \text{ for all } y \in \mathbb{R}, u \neq 0, \text{ so the origin } (0, 0) \text{ is excluded.}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Simultaneous intersection of perpendicular bisector and ray locus with exact surd calculations.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding Cartesian equation of perpendicular bisector.

walkthrough.text:
Expand squared distances:
$$(x - 2)^2 + y^2 = x^2 + (y - 4)^2$$
$$x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 = x^2 + y^2 - 8y + 16$$

Simplify to slope-intercept form:
$$-4x + 4 = -8y + 16 \implies 8y = 4x + 12 \implies y = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{3}{2}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving simultaneously ray and line locus for exact Cartesian coordinates.

walkthrough.text:
State ray equation and equate with line:
$$y = x\sqrt{3} \quad (x > 0)$$
$$x\sqrt{3} = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{3}{2} \implies (2\sqrt{3} - 1)x = 3$$

Rationalise denominator to find exact coordinates:
$$x = \frac{3(2\sqrt{3} + 1)}{(2\sqrt{3} - 1)(2\sqrt{3} + 1)} = \frac{3(2\sqrt{3} + 1)}{12 - 1} = \frac{3 + 6\sqrt{3}}{11}$$
$$y = x\sqrt{3} = \frac{(3 + 6\sqrt{3})\sqrt{3}}{11} = \frac{18 + 3\sqrt{3}}{11}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding exact modulus of intersection point.

walkthrough.text:
Relate modulus to real part:
$$x = |z|\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2}|z| \implies |z| = 2x$$

Calculate exact modulus:
$$|z| = 2\left(\frac{3 + 6\sqrt{3}}{11}\right) = \frac{6 + 12\sqrt{3}}{11}$$
